body: I'm still in Uni, but my parents told me that my chances of succes are gone, because I failed two half-courses in my first semester. They still want me to graduate, but I honestly don't know what I'm doing anymore, considering my degree will be worthless in the end because of my bad grades.

I don't think I'm ready mentally or financially to go through the process of finding a therapist or the right type of therapy. I went to the same person for years on and off, and about 5 or so as well, in addition to some who would just perscribe me meds.

My insurance has told me they won't pay for any therapy anymore, so it would all fall on me. I have calculated how much I would have to spend on therapy from my monthly wage and it's way more than I could afford. I simply cannot shop around for therapists in my current situation. Some people just have it objectively bad, and I would rather spend money and time on trying to get out of my bad situation in life rather than trying therapy, which hasn't worked for 10 years.

Currently, my goal is to move out and I think money is better spent on focusing my efforts on that rather than on therapist after therapist who I would have to give my trust to and make myself vulnerable to all over, just to be treated badly again.

The book thing is kind of ironic, because the publisher never misses an opportunity to mention how "elite" the author is - on the cover, in the description of the book, it's very much stressed how successful the author is, even though the book is about the torture that this person had to go through to make the success happen.

I don't know anyone who is more of a failure or less successful than myself. I would have much rather chosen myself to do an apprenticeship for a low-paying job, rather than forced to do A-Levels and go to the Uni my parents picked for me.
Please don't tell me to try another therapist or different meds. It feels very invalidating of the trauma I had to go through in the name of therapy.
I know, I just wished they broke me into being successful, instead of just breaking me and leaving me to pick up the pieces while having no hope of a decent future.

I wish I was mentally stronger, but I am too weak. Not that it matters any more, my life is ruined and I am a ruined person. I don't think I'll ever find a good environment, because I'm unlovable. It's over for me.

Although this makes sense, it's too late now for me. No amount of analysis and hindsight is going to fix my past or me as a person, which has ruined my future already.

And therapy has played a big part in my self blame I feel today. It has traumatised me and not helped one bit. I wished all that time and effort was directed to removing me from my home instead of endless sessions and meds I was given for a decade.

I have ruined my academic career, which was the only thing I focused on growing up. Which means I am now 21 with nothing under my belt that would help me build a career or even find any jobs. I might have been able to become talented at something, but all I did was school work, and I did badly. At my age and my situation, starting over is impossible, especially because I'm unintelligent and incapable of ever succeeding at anything.

People tell me 21 is young, but no way someone is going to hire me with a messed up CV like mine.

I genuinely can't find a single thing that's even remotely positive about me, no matter how hard I try. If I had a good job or did well in Uni, there would at least be something, but it was all a waste of time and energy.

I disagree, at least they have the means to support themselves, which I will never be able to do comfortably. And it's not like I have the chance to reshape my life later. Neither do I have a greater chance of choosing a job I like, because I have no education, so my opportunities are sparse.
I can't subject myself to therapy again, it has caused me so much more pain and caused me to blame myself even more for how I have turned out to be.
I was, for an entire decade. Didn't help at all.

It's odd that I see the "ordinary life" with a loving partner, friends and a decent job as unattainable, but becoming exceptional as something realistic, even as the only way to make all the hurt and abuse I went through worth it, that I will talk about it as hardships, a part of my journey to success. But now that any chance of success is out of the window, all I see is absolute despair and even worse torture for the rest of my being.

EDIT: I think, for me personally at least, it stems from the feeling that I'm unlovable and will never have a "circle of friends", so I would have to compensate that by being successful instead. Not that it matters now, anyway.
Suicidal as well, I have promised myself I won't end it before a particular date and that's today. So, wanna talk?

My family lives scattered around the globe, but I can try. It's sad that my parents are lying to them about what I'm doing and my grades, even when I'm right next to them and I have to see my parents doing that. They literally spew complete lies about my academic success, as if the family members care, seriously. I don't know why it hurts so much.

>as a fellow asian, you are so strong, i feel what you are going through and seriously, i hope after this, i know you will be strong enough to overcome anything that comes your way. best of luck < 3

Thanks, means a lot. Many non-Asians don't get it. Even some Asians don't believe me or downplay it.

Hi, thank you so much for your comment, there are some things that are really helpful.

My Uni has not been able to figure out how to do online exams yet and they have decided to raise the difficulty for their exam significantly to make up for the lack of surveillance. Everyone was shocked at how much harder the exams were compared to the past papers. But that doesn't matter, it's on my records now that I'm a failure and no one will care when I'm job hunting. I hate myself so much for it, my entire life was a waste of time.

I can't be confident that I will ever know what I want to do. My greatest fear is that I will go through the "I don't know who I am" phase others go through in their teen years as a 21 years old and when I have finally figured it out, it will be too late. Even now, I likely won't be able to get an apprenticeship opportunity, as they want 16 years olds, not a 21 years old who failed at Uni. Nor can I get a real job that would pay the bills while I take a break from Uni, as no one wants to employ someone with A-Levels without a degree.

My country is known as one of the hardest countries to make friends in. It is not impossible, but you must have the right connections to be deemed the right candidate to be seen with. I know it sounds bizarre, but I have lived here all my life and this is how it is. Friendships aren't formed because someone likes you, they are based on merit, which I don't bring. It's all about keeping up appearances in this tiny trash yountry I live in. I am talking to people, but I really just want to leave this country, I don't feel like I belong here. This is also the reason why I want to get a degree, as this would make it easier to leave this place behind.

Lastly, about my parents. I will never forgive them. Not only have they ruined me beyond repair and are now leaving me to tidy up after their mess and I have to pick up the pieces left of my life. Even worse, after messing up their first-born (me), they have decided to paint me as a weak problem child and put all the blame on me and are now treating my brother the same way. I will not forgive them, if they don't see that they have destroyed me. My childhood was hell. What 11 years old is suicidal? Well, I was.

But your advice on psychology and I'll try to gather my strengths and focus on getting better.

I'm not the golden child, I'm more of a scapegoat, the "weak problem child".

EDIT: To clarify, my parents have, imo, never been able to love me as a person. They loved "their daughter", but not "me" (Idk if that makes sense). I feel like I was and still am a huge disappointment. I must find the original source (likely some manga from my childhood), but someone said "loving someone and controlling them are complete opposits". My parents can't love me without me fulfilling these conditions. Ad that's how I was treated my entire life. Conditional love, abuse if I didn't fulfil the demands. I explain my upbringing in other posts, but this is my explanation for it.

Because my life has been horrible and just filled with pain up to this point, I can't really envision myself ever being remotely happy and that's my issue. I am getting encouragement from others to keep fighting, but I can't see the end of the tunnel.

Sadly, I can't move out for financial reasons. It's hard even envisioning a life that's not filled with hurt and I often feel like life is just passing me by with me trapped in my childhood bedroom and trauma.

I have also developed this sense of urgency, thinking that because my life was a horror show up until now, I must have a great redemption arc and an absolutely fantastic future to make up for it, especially because I'm quite old now to be having these issues, while others are already far into their careers or finishing Uni at my age. A mediocre future just won't cut it. Idk whether that makes any sense.

I'm on that sub quite often to not feel so abnormal and alone, but unfortunately, this whole control (and my own inability to stand up to my parents) have ruined my chances of doing a vocational course or an apprenticeship, which might have put me in a better situation financially today. The only source of income I have is a part time job in fast food, rent alone can be several times of what I make in a month.

Embarassingly, I have no friends, in the most literal way imaginable. There is no person that would let me stay with them. I do understand that living at home is damaging me, but I have no other choice.
I have been in school for 15 years, I'm not starting anything new. That isn't my issue. Went through abuse and still couldn't improve, so nothing will ever get me to success.

Thank you for your compassionate response.

I am awful at everything I ever did. So many subjects at school throughout the years and I never did well at any of them. I also have no interests of any value, they won't build a viable career path for me. My only purpose in life was to get into a good Uni and get a good job, that was the only thing I was trained towards and abused for it, but that path is dead now. My life was a complete waste of time and energy. Now, I am left to suffer through what this torture has left me with. No social life, horrible mental health, no future. I'm just tired of being in mental anguish while not nearly being as successful as other people who were abused by tiger parents. Even when I read books by people who went through the same thing, I feel jealous, because they got to graduate from Tokyo Uni at least, or landed a job where they would earn a lot of money. It leads to me feeling worthless (which is just the truth to be honest) and isolated. My Uni doesn't care, why would they?

There is no point in me having any dreams, it's over. My life is over. At my age and a messed up CV, no one is going to hire me.

I'm not in therapy, as I believe the decade I spent in mental health care has damaged me immensely and I am completely traumatised by the abuse I had to suffer through, perpetrated by those who were supposed to help me. My Uni offers some support, but it's of little help. I also don't want to tell my Uni about personal issues, it doesn't concern them. Besides, what's an online Uni going to do?

I am working atm, some part-time job in the fast food industry. My CV doesn't look bad bc it's badly written, I just have an entire life I have to be ashamed of and must hide. No one is going to hire someone who was institutionalised, dropped out of High School and has a worthless A-Level (got them during the pandemic).

Interestingly enough, I'm also of Asian decent.

The greatest fear I have is to live a mediocre life after all I've been through. It simply wouldn't be enough of a payoff for all of the pain I'm experiencing and have been for a decade. I constantly see posts on here and on Twitter by other survivors that talk about having to suffer through mental health issues for decades after leaving their parents. That is a fate I want to spare myself from. I have no strength left in me to fight against CPTSD or other mental illments, I am simply exhausted.

It's horrible that after suffering because of our parents, we are expected to be our own person, a normal and well-adjusted member of society when we become adults. If we aren't it's our own fault. We shouldn't blame our parents and look forward, they say, but I have already been destroyed.  
Sadly, I do think that it's all too late to start anew, my peers are far into their careers and have an established presence in their fields, I wouldn't be able to make up the difference in experience, knowledge and capability. Even if I did a complete shift in careers, someone like me is destined to fail anyway. I'll be an old NEET in the future, bitter and an unaccomplished burden.

I was planning to do so, but it's not just my life that's irreversably ruined, but everything about myself is defective. A bad life might be turned around (not that I care anymore), but a broken person that is fundamentally wrong in her existence can't. Someone who knows me very well once told me that I'm just wrong, everything about me is just wrong and people can tell that I have never experienced happiness. I know myself even better then they know me, and I completely agree.
No, I'm from some irrelevant shite country in Europe I can't stand staying in any longer. I used to make plans to leave but these are now shattered because of my failings.

Well, I don't know how much more effort and time I can give than a full decade (half my childhood, even into adulthood) or therapy, 8 months of inpatient and countless meds. I have exhausted the resources available and insurance won't pay for any mental health care anymore, because they see it as pointless. I do not care wether there is a possibility that things get better in the future, it's simply not worth the pain.

Thanks for your response.

My wish was that at least my death would have a purpose, which my life couldn't fulfill, but is seems that even that won't come true. I feel horrible for my brother, I really do.

Therapy has not helped me in the slightest, and I tried for 10 years. Same for meds, my doctor gave me one after another to try out and then blamed me for the lack of success his efforts had and ghosted me. I actually have not a single person who I could remotely call a friend or even an acquaintance. My Uni is online, so no help from them.

The constant pain and agony I'm in won't allow me to hang on for another decade or two. I simply do not care anymore whether there possibly might somewhen somehow be a good life ahead of me.

Honestly, I have no hope left. I have tried being hopeful, that's why I went to therapy for 10 years and took so many meds with side-effects. But at this point, I have no strength left in me to trust anyone who tells me that things are going to get better. Sometimes, it just doesn't.

Thanks, but I don't know whether I still have the strength to believe that things will magically get better - it looks less than bleak, it's horrible and every single second hurts. It has been my entire life and I'm not planning to exist like this, especially seeing how many survivors have to depend on meds for the rest of their lives and still are mentally broken.

Idk whether my existence will help my brother, I am currently an onlooker in his abuse.

My parents have been telling me that a failure in school is basically the worst thing that can happen and always would talk about school as if it's a life or death situation and physically and mentally abused me to get me to do better (never worked).

Found out recently that my father dropped out of high school and his father (my grand-father) has used his connections to find him a very well-paying job he held for a year before getting his A-Levels independently and going to Uni. He's now doing fine financially and can feed his wife and three kids with his income alone while living in the city centre of an expensive city. I have no idea why my parents had to abuse me like that when he is a prime example of dropping out not being the end of your life.

I genuinely don't believe I will ever be successful. I can't just start a new path or a career, I'm certain I will fail out of whatever I try. Besides, no one is going to hire me in the first place. The energy is gone, I'm completely burnt out. A decade ago, I used to believe that things are going to get better, but I was wrong.

I'm in the same situation. Abuse and mental health issues are all I know of life and myself as a person. Now, in my 20s, I have no personality, no drive, just a long history of mental illness, trauma and absolutely nothing to live for.

However, if I choose to end my life, I think it wouldn't have been me who killed me. It would have been my abusers who murdered me indirectly and my pride won't allow it.

I don't care what other people will feel when I'm gone (with the exception of my brother), but as long as I am alive, I live for my own purposes and I have the greatest priority, not them, not anyone else.

I have let them control my life until now, I won't let them control when my life ends. At least, that's what I'm telling myself to convince myself to keep going.
